create.name: Judith Valente
create.bio:
Judith Valente is a poet, essayist and retreat leader whose spiritual writing grew out of a long career in journalism. She started as a reporter at The Washington Post, later wrote for The Wall Street Journal from Chicago and London, and spent years covering religion for PBS's Religion & Ethics NewsWeekly and for public radio. A lay associate of Mount St. Scholastica, the Benedictine community in Atchison, Kansas, she wrote about her time with the sisters in the memoir Atchison Blue, and the Rule of St. Benedict remains at the centre of her teaching.

Her retreats and talks focus on living contemplatively in an ordinary working life: pausing, paying attention, finding the sacred in small daily things and reading poetry as a spiritual practice. Her books include The Art of Pausing, How to Live, on what Benedict's rule offers people today, How to Be, a conversation with a monk, and The Italian Soul, which looks at Italian habits of slowness and joy as a quiet spiritual discipline. She has also published several collections of poems, most recently How to Be a Contemplative. Since 2023 she has led a small annual pilgrimage to little-known Benedictine places in the Abruzzo region of Italy, and she speaks to Benedictine lay groups, retreat houses and conferences in the United States and abroad.

books.title: The Italian Soul: How to Savor the Full Joys of Life
books.author: Judith Valente
books.description: Part travel writing and part spiritual guide, drawn from her many stays in Italy. It looks at the slower rhythms, hospitality and contemplative attitudes of Italian life and how readers might bring them home.

books.title: How to Be a Contemplative
books.author: Judith Valente
books.description: A collection of her poems, each followed by a short reflection. The poems look for the sacred in ordinary days, meals and objects.

books.title: How to Live: What the Rule of St. Benedict Teaches Us About Happiness, Meaning, and Community
books.author: Judith Valente
books.description: An exploration of the main themes of the sixth-century Rule of St. Benedict for readers today. She draws on her years with a Benedictine community to show how its practices of listening, balance and hospitality can shape daily life.
